title: The One Who's Not Busy, Part 3
speaker: Nomon Tim Burnett
summary: The talk's main teaching emphasizes the importance of letting go of preconceptions and simply being present in the moment, rather than striving for mental clarity or understanding. This is illustrated through the concept of "non-thinking," which refers to a state of engagement with reality without judgment or evaluation. By embracing this approach, practitioners can cultivate compassion and wisdom, and deepen their understanding of themselves and the world around them.

sentences.text: *One morning we will wake up and forget to build that wall we've been building, the one between us, the one we've been building for years, perhaps out of some sense of right and boundary, perhaps out of habit.
One morning we will wake up and let our empty hands hang empty at our sides.
Perhaps they will rise as empty things sometimes do when blown by the wind.
Perhaps they will simply not remember how to grasp, how to rage.
We'll wake up that morning and we will have misplaced all our theories about why and how and who did what to whom.
We will have mislaid all of our timelines of when and plans of what, and we will not scramble to write the plans and theories anew.
And that morning not much else will have changed.*
*Whatever is blooming will still be in bloom.
Whatever is wilting will wilt.
There will be fields to plow and trains to load and children to feed and work to do.
And in every moment, in every action, we will feel the urge to say thank you.
We will follow the urge to bow.*
That's my kind of enlightenment.
Just basically, what if we forgot that we were all messed up?
It just didn't occur to us one day.
